page.layout: One printed page, numbered 99. Running head at top centre above the text. Main text in one column: first a continuation of a poem (Latin verse, italic), then the signature "I. I. B.", then a rule, the division heading "DE POETIS.", a dedication line "AD GVLIELMVM MOGNAEVM" in two lines, and a verse poem below. Note initials "G. ij." at the foot of the verse, right side.

p.i:
Quos nec balsama vindicant odora,
Nec seruant Alabastra foeta Nardo,
Nec quod mittit Arabs & Indus unguen.
Sed totus patet hoc Culex sepulchro
Auri splendidius micante lamna:
Cui nec dente potest nocere tristi
Tempus, nec caries, sitúsve turpis.
Tam belle Culici queunt sepulto
Reges, si licet, inuidere tantum.

NON, si quid Latio ludere pectine
Concessit facilis Pegasidum chorus
Me Gallis cupidum vatibus inserit,
Et Lauros patitur tollere duplices:
Ceu, Mognæe, putas. Lancibus impares
Phœbus spargit opes imparibus suas.
Sunt qui Maonij carminis alite
Heroum celebrant facta potentium,
Et magni altiloquas Virgilij tubas
Inflant non pauidi, belláque disserunt?
Et Martem tunica testum adamantina.
Verum hic mœsta canit, tristibus indicans

page.notes: Right margin carries only the page number 99. Left margin has a small mark/signature near the bottom ("G. ij.", at the lower right of the verse block, treated as a signature in the text). Latin verse lines are set in italic with long s rendered as plain s; "potest" and similar kept as printed. Words ending the verse ("Pegasidum", "Mognae") copied as printed. Note: the signature "G. ij." may be a gathering mark rather than a footnote; it was placed as a foot paragraph. The text "Lauros patitur tollere duplices" and "Lancibus impares" are read directly from the scan.
